evidence: RedisStore._shared_fallback_stores was a plain Python dictionary accessed concurrently by background simulation threads and asynchronous FastAPI request handlers without mutual exclusion locking.
operational_consequence: Risk of RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration when list_values() or list_keys() was called while a simulation run updated metrics or pushed events.
root_cause: The in-memory fallback store was implemented as an unsynchronized class-level dictionary without thread locks.
remediation: Added reentrant lock threading.RLock() to RedisStore class and protected all dictionary reads, writes, deletions, and iterations with with RedisStore._lock:.

evidence: Domain layer explainer directly imported concrete infrastructure modules (app.infrastructure.cache.get_redis_client, httpx) at top level, and module terminology labeled heuristic risk scoring as compute_shap.
operational_consequence: Clean Architecture violation: Domain entities depended on concrete HTTP and cache drivers. Ambiguity between fast SLA heuristic attribution and exact KernelExplainer game-theoretic Shapley values.
root_cause: Historical consolidation of SLA feature attribution into the domain layer without dependency inversion.
remediation: Decoupled top-level infrastructure dependencies; made Redis lookup and webhook delivery use lazy, non-breaking invocations; updated docstrings to clarify heuristic attribution methodology versus full KernelExplainer.

evidence: Source code contained hardcoded candidate password strings ('cfi_redis_secure_pass_2026', 'cfi_redis_secure_pass_2026_change_in_production') in auto-healing connection loops.
operational_consequence: Security audit failure; violated secret management hygiene by embedding static credentials into source code instead of relying strictly on environment configuration.
root_cause: Development convenience logic was introduced to automatically attempt connection using historical placeholder passwords.
remediation: Removed all hardcoded password strings from candidate probing arrays across all four files; connection resolution now strictly honors parsed URL passwords and settings.redis_password.

evidence: Production mode (app_env == 'production') lacked startup fail-fast assertions to reject default placeholder secrets (e.g. payload_signing_secret, postgres_password) or open debug flags.
operational_consequence: A deployment configured with APP_ENV=production could inadvertently start up with insecure development placeholders intact.
root_cause: Configuration validation relied on runtime defaults without an explicit fail-closed production policy.
remediation: Implemented Settings.validate_production_invariants() and integrated it into the FastAPI lifespan startup lifecycle, raising immediate ValueError on insecure production configurations.

evidence: Simulation _stop_events dictionary was stored as an unbounded process-global dictionary without synchronization or memory bounds.
operational_consequence: Potential memory growth over very large numbers of simulation executions in long-running services.
root_cause: Absence of bounded eviction or locking around the background task stop signal collection.
remediation: Introduced _stop_events_lock and automatic LRU bounding to prune completed stop event objects once the collection exceeds 500 entries.
